🇲🇽🎓 <u>For the First Time, the IPN's Own Community Helps Pick Its Director</u>

For decades, the director of Mexico's Instituto Politécnico Nacional was simply appointed from above. This time students, teachers and staff vote first. Candidates register Nov 2-6, and electronic voting across all three sectors runs Nov 25-27. Two shortlists, three women and three men, go in a sealed envelope to President Sheinbaum on December 1.

🇲🇽🍎 <u>Junk Food Is Out of Mexico's Schools: One Year In</u>

A year after the ban took effect, Education Secretary Mario Delgado told lawmakers that junk food is gone from Mexico's basic-education schools. The industry is still fighting it with more than 139 amparo suits. "We expelled junk food from basic-education schools in a single year, and we will keep fighting the big corporations in court so these products don't come back."
banner: SCHOOLS: JUNK FOOD GONE IN ONE YEAR

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Mexico's Legal Diesel Market Posts Its Biggest Jump in a Decade</u>

Mexico's apparent diesel consumption rose 22.2% from January to August, to a record 459.2 thousand barrels a day, according to Sener figures reported by El Economista. The jump coincides with the crackdown on fuel smuggling that began with the seizure of the tanker Challenge Procyon in Tampico in March 2025. Diesel that used to come in mislabeled as lubricant now shows up in the legal market.

Pemex diesel sales grew 18.4% to 320.1 thousand barrels a day, and the share of imports fell from 46.7% to 39.3%.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>UN Adopts Mexico's Resolution Against Arms Trafficking</u>

At the Palermo Convention conference in Vienna, member states unanimously adopted a resolution presented by Mexico and Honduras against illicit firearms trafficking, the Foreign Ministry (SRE) reported. It targets the corruption that lets criminal groups make and move weapons. It also urges governments to trace recovered guns and use that data to map trafficking networks.

Sheinbaum has said 75% of the weapons in Mexico come from the United States. Since October 2024, Mexican forces have seized 36,300 illegal firearms.
banner: UN BACKS MEXICO ON ARMS TRAFFICKING

🇲🇽🕊️ <u>"Hasta Siempre, Ingeniero": Mexico's Government Honors Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas</u>

The government opened Thursday's morning press conference with a farewell to Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas. Sheinbaum called it a deeply felt loss and pointed to his idea of democracy: one "that comes from below, not the democracy of the elites."

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez said the homage also belongs "to those who suffered persecution by an authoritarian regime and to those who lost their lives winning freedoms."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: Taddei Got Her Start Before Morena Even Existed</u>

The opposition wants to hang Guadalupe Taddei on Morena. Sheinbaum went through the record: Taddei took over Sonora's electoral institute in 2014, "when Morena didn't even exist yet," under PAN governor Guillermo Padrés, and the appointment was approved by the INE General Council headed by Lorenzo Córdova.

She reached the INE presidency in 2023 by tómbola, a random draw, because the Chamber of Deputies never reached a two-thirds majority. "If she committed crimes, let it be investigated," Sheinbaum said, and she wants a deep audit of the institute.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Business Council: 23 Stalled Projects Unblocked, $3.9 Billion Moving</u>

Mexico's top business council, the CCE, says domestic investment is finally flowing. Since the leaders of its 14 member associations met President Sheinbaum in early May, 23 stalled projects worth 3.9 billion dollars have been unblocked, CCE president José Medina Mora said.

After 0.5% growth last year, the council now expects 2% this year and 2.5% in 2027. The two bottlenecks it wants fixed are energy supply and water.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US Ambassador: The Terrorist Label Is Not About Bombing Mexico</u>

Ronald Johnson, Washington's ambassador to Mexico, told the Milken Institute's Global Investors Symposium that designating cartels as terrorist organizations does not mean the US wants to "drop bombs on Mexico." He said the label is about financial and legal tools: sanctions and anti-terror-financing measures aimed at traffickers, money launderers and shell companies.

Mexico's position hasn't moved: cooperation, yes. Foreign troops or strikes on Mexican soil, no.
banner: US ENVOY: NO BOMBS ON MEXICO

🇲🇽🇮🇳 <u>Mexico and India Open Trade Talks</u>

Mexico and India formally opened negotiations for a Preferential Trade Agreement on October 28, signing the terms of reference that set its scope and roadmap. A Mexican business mission to India is planned for early 2027.

The numbers show why. In 2025 Mexico sold India $1.97 billion and bought $9.13 billion, a $7.16 billion deficit. Mexican exports to India fell 28% from 2024.

Priority sectors are autos, chemicals, electronics, pharma, agrifood, energy, critical minerals and medical devices. The talks follow up on the deal Sheinbaum and Modi struck at the G7 in June 2025. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🌉 <u>Amado Nervo Bridge Opens Between Jalisco and Nayarit</u>

Sheinbaum opened the Amado Nervo Bridge over the Ameca River on October 28. It links Puerto Vallarta with Bahía de Banderas and cuts travel times by up to 40 minutes.

It cost 963 million pesos and runs more than 800 meters, with three lanes each way and a bike lane. It gives an alternative to Federal Highway 200, which carries about 73,000 vehicles a day. Some 479,000 people benefit.

The bridge is named for a Nayarit poet and was paid for with public money.
